items.title: s464C: repayment redrawn within 30 days (Jordan Hale)
items.question: Was a repayment of at least the s464C amount followed within 30 days by new advances of at least that amount?
items.reasoning: £6,000.00 repaid on 2026-04-20 and £6,000.00 redrawn by 2026-05-10. The repayment is matched to the new advance and does not reduce the s455 charge (s464C(1)).

items.title: AIA shared with an associated company?
items.question: Is this company related to another (common control and shared premises or similar activities), so one AIA is shared?
factors: Are the businesses controlled by the same person(s)?
The shared premises condition - do they carry on qualifying activities from the same premises?
The similar activities condition - is more than 50% of turnover from the same NACE classification?
Groups of companies share one AIA (s51C) regardless of these conditions
items.reasoning: An associated company is recorded. The full AIA is provisionally allocated to this company on the assumption that the related business claims none; the reviewer must confirm the allocation.
items.impact: Changes the AIA available and so the capital allowances claimed.

items.title: Settlements legislation: Alex Okafor
items.question: Is dividend income arising to a spouse, civil partner or minor child from shares that are not an outright gift of ordinary share capital carrying full rights?
factors: Is there an arrangement with an element of bounty (an uncommercial transfer of value)?
Are the shares a separate class (alphabet shares), carry restricted rights, or are dividends waived/varied?
Is the income mainly derived from one person's work in the company?
The s626 exemption for outright gifts between spouses of shares that are not wholly or substantially a right to income
items.reasoning: Alex Okafor holds B shares (a separate class) and connected to d1, who works in the business and does not work in the business. Dividends to them may be taxed on the settlor (ITTOIA s624).

items.title: Use of home - actual cost apportionment: Use of home office - payment to director
items.question: What part of the household costs relates to business use, and is that apportionment reasonable?
factors: Number of rooms used and whether any room is used exclusively for business (CGT private residence relief risk)
Hours of business use against total use
Which costs are fixed (council tax, mortgage interest, rent) and which vary with use (heat, light)
For a company paying a director - is there a written arrangement and evidence of the additional household costs?
Payments up to the employee flat rate per week are exempt without evidence (ITEPA s316A)
items.reasoning: The claim is provisionally allowed for the business. For a company, only the employee flat rate per week is exempt for the director without evidence; any excess is at risk of being taxable earnings.
